sanskrit_verse:
mahāpāpābhiśasto yaḥ pātakāt tartum icchati /
pūrvam aṅgīkṛtaṃ tena jito 'sau daṇḍam arhati // BrhS_1,3.39
transliteration: mahāpāpābhiśasto yaḥ pātakāt tartum icchati / pūrvam aṅgīkṛtaṃ tena jito 'sau daṇḍam arhati //
sph_interpretive_translation: One who is accused of great sin and desires to be purified therefrom must first accept responsibility; having done so, he becomes entitled to corrective restoration.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority stems from conscious assumption of responsibility
Restoration logic operates only upon voluntary integrity alignment
executable_legal_axioms: IF (accused_of_mahapapa = TRUE) AND (desires_purification = TRUE) THEN (responsibility_assumption_required = TRUE)
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, this verse establishes that no judicial proceeding may commence unless the accused has consciously acknowledged their transgression. The court's role is solely facilitative of restoration once such acknowledgment occurs.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa is established by internal validation, not external accusation. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as sequential purification only after self-owned causality. Proportional responsibility aligns with capacity for truth-bearing. Non-punitive reality rule confirms suffering cannot originate in Dharma-adjudicated process.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate Svadharmic Completion Process upon voluntary confession
Assign Tapas-Based Realignments according to individual constitution
Deploy Vedic Witness Protocols to stabilize consciousness shift
Establish Dharmic Accountability Circles led by realized community elders
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, Dharma stands restored. Justice flows from consciousness alone. Reality remains non-punitive. All actions proceed under the supremacy of awakened awareness.
